=== THE DELTA: ONE COMMIT, 14 LINES, AND IT IS A GOOD FIX ===
00f1760 changes `resolve_reviewable_head`'s walk from `git log --format=%H <head>` to `git log --first-parent --format=%H <head>`, matching what `commit_files` already does for a merge.

I DID NOT TAKE THE BUG REPORT ON TRUST -- I REPRODUCED IT DETERMINISTICALLY, ON LINUX. The commit message says the failure was Windows-only and that Linux passed by luck of commit-date ordering. I built the scenario by hand with controlled GIT_COMMITTER_DATEs in a throwaway repo: base -> "substantive on mainline" (t+10s) on the mainline, a side branch off base with its own commit at t+20s, then `git merge -s ours side` at t+30s, so the side-branch commit sorts AFTER the mainline commit under plain commit-date ordering. Then I ran the branch's own resolve_reviewable_head both ways against that repo:
    WITH --first-parent (the fix)  -> 03220ee  CORRECT (the mainline substantive commit)
    WITHOUT (plain git log)        -> 258fd51  *** WRONG: the side branch's own commit ***
So the fix is load-bearing and correct, and the author's root-cause analysis ("Passing on Linux was luck, not correctness -- the underlying walk was already wrong on every platform, just not always observably so") is accurate. I verified it rather than believing it.

=== NEW FINDING: THE FIX HAS NO DETERMINISTIC REGRESSION TEST ===
MEASURED: I reverted `--first-parent` back to the plain walk and ran the full suite on Linux -> **89 passed, 0 failed** in tests/test_lwb_lanes.py, and the whole suite is green too. Nothing in this repo's tests catches a revert of this fix on Linux.
The only test that ever discriminated (test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff) does so by accident of commit-date ordering -- which is exactly why it failed on Windows and passed on Linux in the first place. So the guard is non-deterministic on EVERY platform, not just absent on Linux: it happens to catch the bug where timestamps tie and happens to miss it where they don't. A fix whose regression test only fires on a timing coincidence is one refactor away from silently regressing.
This is squarely the "is the check that guards this vacuous?" question this repo keeps getting bitten by, and it is worth closing because the fix is otherwise excellent. The scenario I built above is the deterministic test: set explicit GIT_COMMITTER_DATE values so the side-branch commit MUST sort ahead of the mainline commit under the default walk, then assert resolve_reviewable_head returns the mainline commit. That test fails without --first-parent and passes with it, on every platform, regardless of clock resolution. NOT BLOCKING -- the fix itself is right and proven -- but recommended as a follow-up commit on this branch, since it is cheap and this PR is precisely the one about making lanes-resolution correct.

- ADVERSARIAL CHECK ON THE FIX ITSELF: does --first-parent skip something substantive? No. A merge's second-parent content is never visited by the walk, but the MERGE COMMIT itself stands in for all of it, because commit_files reports a merge's first-parent diff -- i.e. everything that merge introduced. So a merge that brings in real content is not record-only, the walk stops there, and the reviewable head is the merge. Consistent with #56's own design rather than in tension with it.
